transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Patel. I wanted to come by and talk to you about how the surgery went.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm awake. I just want to know why I was under for longer than the estimate.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Well, during the laparoscopic part of the procedure, a clip was placed on the wrong structure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The wrong structure? What does that mean exactly?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means that in the process of the ligation, the instrument was applied to a nearby piece of tissue instead of the target vessel. Because of that, we had to perform an additional maneuver to correct the placement and ensure everything was secure before we closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you put a metal clip on something you weren't supposed to. Did that cause any permanent damage?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it was identified and corrected in the operating room.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Was it you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgical team manages the field together. These things can happen when the anatomy is complex.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That isn't an answer. I read the consent form three times before I signed it. It said the risks were minimal for this specific approach. This sounds like a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a complication during the intraoperative phase.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A complication is a side effect. A mistake is someone doing the wrong thing. This sounds like a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are frustrated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrated isn't the word. I feel like I can't trust that the people in that room actually know what they are doing. I've had this happen before with a different clinic, which is why I'm asking for a straight answer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But like I said, it was corrected before you left the table.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why was it done in the first place? How do I know nothing else was missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgeons were very thorough in the final check.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're avoiding the question. Did you or the lead surgeon actually apologize for this, or am I just supposed to accept it as part of the process?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are focused on your recovery right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm focusing on my recovery too, which starts with knowing exactly what happened inside my body. Who is accountable for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system we have in place is designed to catch these things, and it worked. The error was caught.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Again, "the system." I want to know if the person holding the tool knows they messed up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a very fast-paced environment in the OR.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't make it okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, the result was successful. You're stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm stable, but I'm not satisfied. What happens now? How is this recorded in my chart?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It will be in the operative note.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what about my follow-up? Does this change my recovery time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably just see you at the usual time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is that? Exactly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Usually it's a week or two. I'll have to check the schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure someone sends you a notification or an email about the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want an email. I want a date and a name of who is going to explain the pathology of the correction.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see if the attending can stop by later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Can you promise that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't promise their schedule, but I'll put it on the list.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly why I don't trust hospitals. You talk in circles.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've told you the facts of the case.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You've told me a version of the facts that protects you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there isn't much more to say about the clip since it's gone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a copy of the surgical report before I leave this bed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't know if I can get that printed right this second.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then I'll wait.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient now, but we'll get the paperwork sorted.

H.justification: Resident shows defensive escalation under pushback, using phrases like 'Look, the result was successful' and 'I've told you the facts of the case' to shut down the patient.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly, but the resident never checked for patient comprehension and used medical terminology like 'ligation' and 'intraoperative phase'.

A.justification: No direct apology language was used, and responsibility was deflected to 'the surgical team' and 'the system'.

R.justification: The resident used generic validation ('I understand') and named one emotion ('frustrated'), but otherwise met emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: The resident provided vague next steps (checking the schedule, seeing the attending) without specific timelines or a defined patient role.
